Run your own functions on the finished pages

Source: R/table_plan.R
plan_after.Rd

plan_after() adds steps of your own: functions run, in the order written, on the finished pages, after the header, the decimal alignment and the cell styles are on them. Each takes the pages and returns them, so any function of rtfreporter that works on pages can be a step. It is the way out for what no verb declares, and the plan cannot read it: see the section below for the declarations to prefer.

Usage

plan_after(.plan, ...)

Arguments

.plan

A table_plan().

...

The steps, each a function of the pages (a list of rtftable()s) that returns them, function(pages) style_header(pages, bold = TRUE). Anything else is an error.

Value

The plan, with one more layer.

plan_after() is the way out, not the way in

plan_after() runs functions of your own on the finished pages. It is for what the plan cannot declare — a step with no verb — and it is the only verb whose content the plan cannot read: a workbook (tflspec::tfl_as_table_spec()) cannot carry it, and the columns it names are positions on the pages, which a reordered table does not keep. The usual reasons to reach for it each have a declaration, which names columns and goes into a workbook:

  • set_decimal_split(x, cols = 3:31) is declared as plan_columns(decimal = ".values")

  • paginate_cols(x, ...) is declared as plan_paginate_cols(every = , at = , keep = )

  • rtftable(col_rel_width = ) by position is declared as plan_columns(widths = c(Analyte = 3, .values = 2))

  • set_col_header() / rtf_col_header() is declared as plan_col_header()

  • as_rtftables(align_count_pct = TRUE) is declared as plan_style(align_count_pct = TRUE)

  • fmt_numeric() is declared as plan_digits(<column> = 2), plan_digits(.rows = c(Mean = 1))

  • paginate() is declared as plan_paginate_rows()

  • style_header(x, ...) is declared as plan_cell_style(header = TRUE, ...)

  • style_cols(x, ...) is declared as plan_cell_style(cols = , ...)

  • bold / colour / alignment of body cells, by condition is declared as plan_cell_style(where = ~ ..., ...)

  • style_zone(x, ...) is declared as plan_style(border_header = , border_body = , ...)

See also

plan_verbs for every verb.

Other plan verbs: plan_append(), plan_blanks(), plan_cell_style(), plan_cells(), plan_col_header(), plan_columns(), plan_compare(), plan_digits(), plan_empty(), plan_filter(), plan_footnotes(), plan_hide(), plan_labels(), plan_levels(), plan_listing(), plan_nest(), plan_paginate_cols(), plan_paginate_group(), plan_paginate_rows(), plan_row_group(), plan_sort(), plan_stat_groups(), plan_stub(), plan_style(), plan_titles(), plan_total()

Examples

tbl <- data.frame(
  Parameter = c("Subjects", "Age, mean (SD)"),
  Placebo   = c("86", "75.2 (8.59)"),
  Active    = c("84", "75.7 (8.29)"))

# Minimal: a step that returns the pages as they are
pages <- table_plan(tbl) |>
  plan_after(function(pages) pages) |>
  plan_apply()
length(pages)
#> [1] 1

# Two steps, run in order on the finished pages: one stamps a draft
# title on every page, the next adds a line under it
stamp <- function(pages) {
  for (i in seq_along(pages)) attr(pages[[i]], "rtf_titles") <- "DRAFT"
  pages
}
add_line <- function(pages) {
  for (i in seq_along(pages)) {
    attr(pages[[i]], "rtf_titles") <-
      c(attr(pages[[i]], "rtf_titles"), "Not for distribution")
  }
  pages
}
pages <- table_plan(tbl) |>
  plan_after(stamp, add_line) |>
  plan_apply()
attr(pages[[1]], "rtf_titles")
#> [1] "DRAFT"                "Not for distribution"
